name: Shalmai
title: Assyrian king mentioned in connection with the destruction of Samaria
summary: Shalmai is an Assyrian king mentioned in the book of Hosea in connection with the destruction of Beth-Arbel. He is referred to as an example of brutal warfare and God's judgment on Israel for their apostasy and idolatry. His name is used prophetically as a warning of the coming destruction that would strike the Northern Kingdom of Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Destruction of Beth-Arbel
keyEvents.description: Shalmai is mentioned as the one who destroyed Beth-Arbel on the day of battle, where mothers were crushed together with their children. This event is used by the prophet Hosea as a warning to Israel.

keyEvents.title: Hosea's Warning to Israel
keyEvents.description: The prophet Hosea uses Shalmai's brutal destruction as an image of what would happen to Israel because of their evil and turning away from God.

keyEvents.title: The Context of Israel's Sin
keyEvents.description: Shalmai's destruction is mentioned in a broader context where Hosea condemns Israel's breach of trust by relying on their own strength and many warriors rather than the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Judgment on Bethel
keyEvents.description: The destruction associated with Shalmai is used as a parallel to the coming judgment on Bethel and its idolatry, where Israel's calf images would be removed.
